response.title: How many 48 volt lithium batteries and solar panels do I need for a weekend cabin with a fridge, lights, TV and a well pump?
response.answer:
For a weekend cabin running a refrigerator, lights, TV, and well pump, I'd recommend starting with:

48V LITHIUM BATTERIES

2–3

100Ah LiFePO4 batteries

SOLAR PANELS

4–6

400W panels

SOLAR ARRAY

1,600–2,400W

INVERTER

3,000–5,000W

This is a reasonable starting estimate for a small off-grid cabin with a conventional efficient refrigerator, LED lights, a TV, and an intermittently running well pump. The final size depends heavily on your pump, sunlight, and whether you want to operate through cloudy weekends.

Allowing for inverter and system losses, plan for approximately 3–3.3 kWh per day, or 6–6.6 kWh for a two-day weekend.

2. Battery capacity

A 48V 100Ah lithium battery (commonly 51.2V nominal LiFePO4) stores approximately 5.12 kWh.

Assuming four peak-sun-hours per day and 75% overall solar-system efficiency:

The well pump may determine which inverter you need. A 240V deep-well pump can require substantially more starting power than a refrigerator or TV.

Check its horsepower, voltage, and starting-current specifications. A 120V-only inverter will not operate a 240V pump directly. Choose an inverter with the correct output voltage and sufficient motor-starting surge capacity.

For a weekend cabin running a **refrigerator, lights, TV, and well pump**, I'd recommend starting with:

<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <grid columns={2} gap={3}>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">48V LITHIUM BATTERIES</text>
      <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>2–3</title>
      <text size="sm">100Ah LiFePO4 batteries</text>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">SOLAR PANELS</text>
      <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>4–6</title>
      <text size="sm">400W panels</text>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">SOLAR ARRAY</text>
      <title size="lg">1,600–2,400W</title>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">INVERTER</text>
      <title size="lg">3,000–5,000W</title>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
</box>

This is a reasonable starting estimate for a small off-grid cabin with a conventional efficient refrigerator, LED lights, a TV, and an intermittently running well pump. The final size depends heavily on your pump, sunlight, and whether you want to operate through cloudy weekends.

## 1. Estimated daily electricity usage

| Appliance | Typical daily consumption |
|---|---:|
| Refrigerator | 1,200 Wh |
| LED lights (6) | 240 Wh |
| TV (4 hours) | 400 Wh |
| Well pump | 600 Wh |
| Miscellaneous / standby | 200 Wh |
| **Total** | **2,640 Wh** |

Allowing for inverter and system losses, plan for approximately **3–3.3 kWh per day**, or **6–6.6 kWh for a two-day weekend**.

## 2. Battery capacity

A 48V 100Ah lithium battery (commonly 51.2V nominal LiFePO4) stores approximately 5.12 kWh.

| Batteries | Nominal storage | Approx. usable at 90% discharge |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 × 100Ah | 5.12 kWh | 4.6 kWh |
| 2 × 100Ah | 10.24 kWh | 9.2 kWh |
| 3 × 100Ah | 15.36 kWh | 13.8 kWh |

**Two batteries** should cover a typical two-day weekend even with little solar production, assuming the estimated loads are accurate. Three provide more reserve for cloudy conditions and longer stays.

## 3. How much solar power will you generate?

Assuming four peak-sun-hours per day and 75% overall solar-system efficiency:

{@body const [panels,setPanels] = DIL.useState(5)}
{@body const [sun,setSun] = DIL.useState(4)}
{@body const daily = panels*400*sun*.75/1000}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    **400W solar panels**
    <title size="lg" tabularNums>{panels} panels</title>
  </row>
  <slider min={2} max={10} step={1} value={panels} onChange={setPanels}/>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    **Peak sun-hours per day**
    <title size="lg" tabularNums>{sun} hours</title>
  </row>
  <slider min={2} max={6} step={0.5} value={sun} onChange={setSun}/>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">ESTIMATED DAILY SOLAR PRODUCTION</text>
  <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{daily.toFixed(1)} kWh</title>
  <box background="surface-tertiary" height="12px" radius="full" clip>
    <box background={daily>=3.3?"success-solid":"#D6A04A"} width={`${Math.min(100,daily/3.3*100)}%`} height="100%" radius="full"/>
  </box>
  <row justify="between" align="center">
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Estimated daily requirement: 3.3 kWh</text>
    <text color={daily>=3.3?"success":"secondary"} weight="medium" size="xs">{daily>=3.3?"Meets average demand":"Below average demand"}</text>
  </row>
  <caption>Illustrative production, not a weather forecast. Winter, shade, and cloudy days can significantly reduce output. <Cite refs={["turn377460search0","turn377460search10"]}/></caption>
</box>

## 4. Important: Your well pump

The well pump may determine which inverter you need. A 240V deep-well pump can require substantially more starting power than a refrigerator or TV.

Check its horsepower, voltage, and starting-current specifications. A 120V-only inverter will not operate a 240V pump directly. Choose an inverter with the correct output voltage and sufficient motor-starting surge capacity.

## 5. Four questions to size your system accurately

{@body const [location,setLocation] = DIL.useState("Sunny California / Southwest")}
{@body const [pump,setPump] = DIL.useState("unknown")}
{@body const [fridge,setFridge] = DIL.useState("full")}
{@body const [usage,setUsage] = DIL.useState("weekend")}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <form gap={3} onSubmit={()=>GenUI.issueNewTurn("Please refine my off-grid cabin solar system sizing. Climate/location: "+location+". Well pump: "+pump+". Refrigerator: "+fridge+". Usage: "+usage+". Give me the recommended number of 48V 100Ah LiFePO4 batteries, 400W solar panels, and inverter specifications.")}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Where is your cabin located?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={location} onChange={setLocation}>
        <radio value="Sunny California / Southwest">Sunny California / Southwest</radio>
        <radio value="Midwest / East Coast">Midwest / East Coast</radio>
        <radio value="Pacific Northwest / cloudy area">Pacific Northwest / cloudy area</radio>
        <radio value="Other / not sure">Other / not sure</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>What size is your well pump?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={pump} onChange={setPump}>
        <radio value="0.5 HP">½ HP</radio>
        <radio value="0.75 HP">¾ HP</radio>
        <radio value="1 HP or larger">1 HP or larger</radio>
        <radio value="unknown">Not sure</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>What type of refrigerator?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={fridge} onChange={setFridge}>
        <radio value="full">Full-size household refrigerator</radio>
        <radio value="mini">Mini fridge</radio>
        <radio value="efficient DC">Efficient DC / solar refrigerator</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Will the refrigerator run when you're away?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={usage} onChange={setUsage}>
        <radio value="weekend">Only on weekends</radio>
        <radio value="fridge runs all week">Yes, refrigerator runs all week</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button block submit>Calculate my recommended system <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>

The refrigerator's weekday operation is particularly important: if it runs continuously, you'll need enough solar power to sustain it even when nobody is at the cabin. If you shut everything off between visits, you can often use a smaller system.
